summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass false, scientific_gate_pass false, independently_verified false). Studio did not run: the simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false and comparison_valid is false. The selected scenario is DTaPO dynamic thermal management (task migration plus DVFS) on a 64-core NoC many-core with 32 active and 32 dark cores in a chessboard pattern, evaluated with the LifeSim chain (Sniper, McPAT, HotSpot transient). The proposed experiment was custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, which fails the requirement of 1-128 blocks plus a power object. No Studio result, temperature field or trace exists, so nothing can be compared to the paper. The paper's quantities (an average peak temperature reduction of up to 10.8 C versus DVFS-only, up to 13.6 C versus OSP, about 5 C for chessboard versus contiguous placement) are differences from closed-loop transient runs. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and could not reproduce them even if it had run. Only qualitative reasoning is defensible: spreading active cores over dark neighbors tends to lower peak temperature, and migration and DVFS trade performance for thermal margin. This is not a Studio-validated finding, and no exact replication is claimed. The verdict is a gate-controlled non-applicability and not a confirmation or refutation of the paper's results.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated result and comparison_valid is false.
No per-block x/y coordinates are published; only the 2.95 mm tile size and the 8x8 layout are given, and Figure 4 is illustrative.
No per-core power in watts is published for any application, DVFS level or core state; the 42 W TDP is only an OSP comparison constraint and must not be split into block powers.

The paper's scenario is dynamic and closed-loop (migration, DVFS, wake-up latency, penalties), with transient max/avg/min percentile temperatures averaged over ten runs and four applications; a steady single-power-map run does not match the regime or aggregation.
Power comes from Sniper and McPAT traces; L3 power is excluded from the HotSpot input and dark cores carry static power only, which does not match any static power map.

The published HotSpot package (CBGA-style stack, 0.15 mm silicon, 20 um TIM at 4 W/mK, spreader, heat sink, ambient 318.15 K) may differ from any bundled Studio package; the Studio package assumptions were not supplied, so absolute temperatures would not be comparable.
Spreader and heat sink dimensions, the control period length and the full HotSpot configuration are missing.

Figure 10, 9 and 12 values are not digitized, and the text gives only temperature differences (10.8 C, 13.6 C, about 5 C) with different workload sets and baselines, so no numerical comparison is valid.
No code, data or repository links exist, so no pinned-version asset evidence is available.
Evidence rows lack valid page or pinned-asset locators according to the gate, adversarial code, parameter, config and data checks are unresolved, and independent page review is pending.

The paper's controller and optimizer (a threshold heuristic) are not represented in Studio, and no reliability result is reported, so nothing here supports or contradicts the paper's performance claims.
